title: US Air Force Pilot Requirements 2026: Age, Degree & AFOQT
metaDescription: US Air Force pilot requirements for 2026: age limits, bachelor's degree, AFOQT and TBAS scores, vision and medical standards, plus the path to training.
headline: US Air Force Pilot Requirements 2026: Complete Guide

sections.title: Who Can Become an Air Force Pilot
sections.content:
To become a United States Air Force pilot you must first become a commissioned officer, which requires United States citizenship and a bachelor's degree from an accredited university. The degree can be in any subject, although science, technology, engineering and mathematics degrees are common among successful applicants.

Officers reach the Air Force through the Air Force Academy, Air Force ROTC during university, or Officer Training School after graduation. Applicants must generally be selected for undergraduate pilot training before their 33rd birthday, so starting early gives you time for testing, medical checks and a training slot.

sections.title: Tests, Vision and Medical Standards
sections.content:
Pilot candidates take the Air Force Officer Qualifying Test, a long aptitude exam covering verbal, quantitative and aviation knowledge, plus the Test of Basic Aviation Skills, which measures coordination, spatial awareness and multitasking. The two scores, together with any civilian flying hours, produce a Pilot Candidate Selection Method score.

Medical standards are strict: candidates need a Flying Class I physical, distance vision of 20/70 in each eye correctable to 20/20, and no history of asthma, hay fever or allergies after the age of 12. Height must fall within the cockpit range of roughly 64 to 77 inches standing.

sections.title: Training Path and Service Commitment
sections.content:
Selected candidates attend Undergraduate Pilot Training, a programme of about a year that moves from classroom academics and simulators to real aircraft, followed by advanced training on a specific aircraft type such as fighters, tankers or transport aircraft. Survival training and mission qualification come next.

After earning their wings, pilots owe about ten years of active-duty service. The long commitment reflects the cost of training, but it also brings steady pay, flight hours on advanced aircraft and a clear path to senior leadership roles.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for US Air Force pilots in 2026?
faqs.a: Pilot candidates must generally be selected for undergraduate pilot training before their 33rd birthday, and waivers beyond that age are rare and discretionary. Because commissioning, testing, medical qualification and security clearance all take months, strong applicants usually begin the process in their early twenties to leave room for delays.

faqs.q: Do you need a specific degree to become an Air Force pilot?
faqs.a: No, the Air Force requires a bachelor's degree but does not mandate a particular major, so graduates in history, business or engineering can all compete for pilot slots. Competitive candidates usually hold a grade point average of 3.0 or higher, and aviation or STEM backgrounds can help with the aptitude tests and early training.

faqs.q: What AFOQT score do pilots need?
faqs.a: Pilot candidates must score at least 25 on the pilot composite of the Air Force Officer Qualifying Test, plus at least 10 on the navigator composite and a combined pilot-navigator score of 50. Competitive applicants typically score far higher, often in the 80th percentile or above, because pilot slots are limited and selection is competitive.

faqs.q: Can you become a pilot with glasses or contact lenses?
faqs.a: Yes, you can qualify with corrected vision as long as your uncorrected distance vision is 20/70 or better in each eye and corrects to 20/20. Laser eye surgery such as PRK or LASIK may also be acceptable after a waiting period and a waiver review, so candidates should confirm their exact situation with a flight surgeon.
